chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Playing a black and tan after-hours club on 18th Street with Elbert Topps
summary: As a young boy Collins played with his mother and Elbert Topps at an after-hours spot whose star was female impersonator Gloria Swanson.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Yeah. Elbert Topps, I'm glad you mentioned that because my mother played piano with Elbert Topps, and I was very young. As a matter of fact I shouldn't have been in a club, but we played a club on 18th Street and in this band was Dan Grissom, and we had a drummer -- his name was -- oh, he was a little popeyed guy.
Yeah. But this was an interesting place, it was an after hour joint. And all the stars came to this. It was a -- we called it in those days a black and tan. That meant white and --
Yeah, okay. So they had an entertainer there who was a female impersonator, a big, black guy who wore a dress. And his name was Gloria Swanson. Like Hi-Fi White.

Oh, yes, but he was a tremendous entertainer. And we worked there for quite a while. All the stars from the loop, you know, the shows or clubs would come there. And I never will forget, Albert Topps was one of the most beautiful guys, I don't know how I could have forgotten him. He was so --
